summary.description: Copper is a reddish-brown metal known for its excellent conductivity of heat and electricity. Its compounds are typically blue or green and used in a range of applications from electronics to agriculture.
emission_sources: Burning of fossil fuels in power plants
environmental_impact: Can accumulate in organisms and become toxic at high concentrations
Toxic to some aquatic species and certain soil micro-organisms
Can disrupt nutrient cycling processes in soils

top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Copper emissions result from various industrial and agricultural processes, and improper management can lead to toxic accumulation in ecosystems. Promoting sustainable production and disposal practices is essential.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Copper contamination in water sources, especially at local scales, can harm aquatic life and reduce water quality, making effective water sanitation practices necessary.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Copper can accumulate in aquatic organisms and disrupt ecosystems, posing a threat to marine biodiversity and ecosystem stability.
